osmoments

The means, variances and covariances of order statistics, the sorted values of a sample, are what the standard error of a sample quantile, the variance of a range, or the best linear estimator of a mean from a five-number summary are built from. Printed tables of the covariances of normal order statistics stop at n = 50 in the sources we found, and the software we found gives the moments of single order statistics or approximates the covariances of the normal by a series. osmoments computes the exact means, variances and covariances of order statistics, at any ranks and any sample size, by numerical evaluation of the defining integrals. Five families are built in, the normal, uniform, exponential, logistic and Gumbel, and any other continuous distribution enters through its distribution, density and quantile functions. On top of the moments it gives those of sample quantiles and of any linear combination of order statistics, and Lloyd’s best linear unbiased estimators of location and scale.

The package has two requirements: the distribution must be continuous, and a moment is computed only if it exists, which the package checks rank by rank from the declared tail indices. The integrals are evaluated on the log scale with the integration range split around the peak of each order statistic’s density, so a few ranks at a sample size in the thousands cost about as much as at n = 20, while a full covariance matrix grows with the square of n. Where a family has closed forms, they are returned instead of the quadrature.

The package’s tests check the quadrature against four kinds of evidence. The closed forms of the uniform and the exponential are reproduced at the minimum, quartiles, median and maximum and all their pairs for n = 20, 100 and 1001 within 1e-10. The ten-decimal normal tables of Tietjen, Kahaner and Beckman (1976) are reproduced within their stated accuracy of 1e-7 on the entries that are printed correctly. Harter’s (1960) moments of the normal range are reproduced within 2e-8. The identities that hold on a complete set of ranks are satisfied within 1e-9. The vignette states each check and its limits.

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ZWuLab/osmoments", build_vignettes = TRUE)

Example 

library(osmoments)

# the means and the covariance matrix of the minimum, the quartiles and the maximum
# of 25 standard normal observations
m <- os_moments(n = 25, ranks = c(1, 7, 13, 19, 25), dist = "norm")
m$alpha
m$B

# the same ranks for a logistic distribution with location 10 and scale 2
os_moments(25, ranks = c(1, 7, 13, 19, 25), dist = "logis", location = 10, scale = 2)

# the standard deviation of the median of an even-sized normal sample
qw <- os_quantile_weights(p = 0.5, n = 10)
sqrt(os_lin_moments(qw$W, os_moments(10, ranks = qw$ranks))$var)

# Lloyd's BLUE of the mean and the standard deviation from a five-number summary
os_blue(m)

A distribution that is not built in enters through os_dist(), with its distribution, density and quantile functions and the tail indices that decide which moments exist:

t5 <- os_dist(
  p = function(q, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE) pt(q, 5, lower.tail = lower.tail, log.p = log.p),
  d = function(x, log = FALSE) dt(x, 5, log = log),
  q = function(p) qt(p, 5),
  symmetric = TRUE, tail = c(5, 5), name = "t5"
)
os_moments(5, dist = t5)

The vignette walks through the families, a user-supplied distribution, the linear layer, what the result holds and how the integrals are evaluated. It is at https://zwulab.github.io/osmoments/ and, after the installation above, vignette("osmoments").

Citation

The paper that describes the package, its verification and the comparison with other software is

Wu, Z. and Tong, T. (2026). osmoments: Exact means, variances and covariances of order statistics in R. Manuscript.

citation("osmoments") prints this reference.

References

Harter, H. L. (1960). Tables of range and studentized range. The Annals of Mathematical Statistics, 31(4), 1122-1147.

Tietjen, G. L., Kahaner, D. K. and Beckman, R. J. (1976). Variances and covariances of the normal order statistics for sample sizes 2 to 50. Report LA-6482-MS, Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory.
